messages:
lee: quick fyi — i just saw deploy-bot pick `2.4.1+backport.20250209.sha9f7` as latest for staging even though the UI shows `2.4.2+docs.20250210.shabb2` at the top. anyone know why? :confused:

dev-bot: deploy-bot: selection logic = highest semver core (major.minor.patch) then highest buildmeta timestamp if semver core ties. display ordering is separate.

ana: so 2.4.2 has higher core but why would bot pick 2.4.1 then?

lee: because the 2.4.2 in UI was a docs-only tag without artifact metadata in CI, so buildmeta timestamp missing. deploy-bot fell back to comparing core+buildmeta and chose backport with explicit timestamp.

tom: that's a bad surprise. humans looked at top-of-list and assumed router would pick it. we need to make pinning explicit and less index-based.

ops-bot: agreed. proposal: change default UI hint to "Router picks by semver core + artifact ts — confirm tag string before pinning" and surface a one-click copy tag button. also make deploy-bot warn when user pins by list index rather than tag.

lee: can we standardize tags so docs-only releases always include a `display_ts` (CI timestamp) even if no binary? that would avoid missing metadata.

docs-bot: we can. CI can attach `display_ts` and `artifact_present=false` to the release metadata. release-notes generator will prefer display_ts for ordering.

ana: another related ask: what about semver increment policy for quick fixes vs backports? are we allowed to create 2.4.2 for docs-only and then later backport 2.4.2 with binary? we had collisions before.

tom: policy we used in the last sprint: reserve semver patch number for any release (binary or docs). if a docs-only tag claims 2.4.2 and later a binary needs that patch, we should either: 1) retag binary to 2.4.2+build.timestamp and mark docs tag as 2.4.2+meta.docs.timestamp (allowed), or 2) bump binary to 2.4.3 if 2.4.2 was consumed by stable channels. we need clear guidelines.

ops-bot: practical rule: core semver uniqueness across stable channels. allow metadata collisions but ensure people pin by full tag string. if you must reserve a patch for docs only, prefer adding `+docs` metadata and set display_ts so it appears but router still sees core equality (router resolves by core then buildmeta ts).

lee: so router behavior = core compare first; if same core and multiple tags, pick the artifact with the latest artifact timestamp. if artifacts missing, fall back to tag creation time. that should be deterministic.

ana: i still worry about human mistakes during rollback windows. can we add a simple CLI helper: `deploy-bot rollback --list` that shows both UI order and router choice side-by-side, with copyable tag strings?

dev-bot: feature accepted, adding `--show-routing-key` flag. sample output:

```
1) UI: 2.4.2+docs.20250210.shabb2  (display_ts: 2025-02-10T12:03Z)
   Router key: 2.4.1 (picked because artifact_ts: 2025-02-09T23:40Z)
2) UI: 2.4.1+backport.20250209.sha9f7  (display_ts: 2025-02-09T23:40Z)  <-- router picks this
```

tom: love that. small UX nit: show an explicit "routing priority" badge in console per row: `router: core+artifact_ts` vs `display: display_ts`.

ops-bot: one more ops constraint: during change windows we should prevent docs-only tags from being auto-promoted to release channels. add a guard in the release workflow that requires `artifact_present=true` or explicit override by release lead.

lee: agreed. let's also add a lint in CI that rejects nonstandard semver metadata (no extra `+` separators, only allowed chars in metadata). we had tags like `2.4.3+meta+oops` once and tools choked.

ana: can we capture these decisions into a tiny RFC? i'll draft: sections — (1) router selection algorithm, (2) UI sorting vs routing, (3) tag metadata conventions, (4) CI lint rules, (5) deploy-bot CLI improvements, (6) change-window guard.

dev-bot: flagging: please include migration steps for existing tags without display_ts. release-notes job will fallback to created_at but RFC should recommend backfilling where possible.

ops-bot: runbook addendum: always verify the exact tag string before a rollback during change windows. if console top != router pick, abort and call release lead. saved us last rollover.

lee: ok putting this to action items:
- ana: draft RFC + examples (2.4.2 docs-only vs binary backport scenarios)
- tom: add CLI `--show-routing-key` and index-vs-tag warning
- docs-bot: make release-note template show normalized label `2.4.2 (docs · 2025-02-10 · sha:bb2)`
- ops-bot: add change-window guard to release workflow
- dev-bot: add semver metadata lint job

ana: will send RFC link once drafted. thanks everyone. closing thread and moving discussion to RFC PR.

tom: thanks — will ping when CLI branch ready.

ops-bot: noted. closing on my end.
